Every device has its own unique HWID. VPN providers use it to identify which device is connected to the subscription and may restrict access if the device limit is reached. By spoofing the identifier, you can bypass this restriction by entering the HWID of any device already connected to the subscription.

When requesting subscriptions, all VPN apps report information about themselves to the provider (usually name and version). Happwner lets you request subscriptions on behalf of any app allowed by the VPN provider.

Every Xray config in the response becomes one Mihomo YAML configuration: proxies, proxy groups, routing and DNS.


Protocols converted:
VLESS (including xtls-rprx-vision, REALITY and post-quantum mlkem768x25519plus encryption), VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, SOCKS, HTTP, WireGuard, Hysteria, Hysteria2 and TUIC.

Transports:
raw/tcp (including the HTTP masquerade), ws, httpupgrade, http/h2, grpc, xhttp/splithttp (with extra, xmux and downloadSettings) and mkcp for VMess. TLS, REALITY, ECH, uTLS fingerprints and certificate pinning (pinnedPeerCertSha256, pinnedPeerCertificateChainSha256) are carried over; where a config lists several pins, Mihomo accepts one, so the first is used.

Also carried:
• verifyPeerCertInNames becomes name-cert-verify, and the mKCP read/write buffers are converted from megabytes to the bytes Mihomo counts.

Routing:
Your own rules are converted, not replaced: domains (full:, domain:, regexp:, geosite: and bare keywords), addresses (CIDR, geoip:, negated geoip:!, private ranges), ports, source address and port, network, users and inbound tags. Conditions that must all hold become AND, alternatives become OR. freedom becomes DIRECT, blackhole becomes REJECT, and a balancer becomes its group. domainStrategy: AsIs adds no-resolve, so address rules do not look the name up first.

geosite: and geoip: stay as they are — Mihomo carries its own databases and downloads them itself, so no lists or URLs are written into the config.

DNS:
Servers become nameserver; a server limited to certain domains becomes nameserver-policy; hosts and fakedns (with the pool it named) carry over; queryStrategy sets ipv6.

Load balancers:
An Xray balancer becomes a single proxy group named after the config\'s remarks, so the balanced servers are offered as one entry rather than separately.

Profiles skipped:
• quic transport for VLESS/VMess/Trojan;
• h2 and xhttp for Trojan, mkcp for anything but VMess;
• gRPC multiMode, REALITY mldsa65Verify;
• the vlite and mtproto protocols;
• Shadowsocks with a method Mihomo does not implement.

Options left out:
• grpc converts, but authority and multiMode have no equivalents — the node runs in single mode.
• Mux.Cool — Mihomo multiplexes by another protocol, so the node connects without multiplexing; only the XUDP packet encoding is kept;
• routing by protocol (bittorrent and the like) and by attrs — Mihomo has no rule for either, and a rule keeps matching without that condition;
• ext: categories — they name an Xray data file this core cannot read;
• DNS expectIPs, and regexp: as a nameserver-policy key;
• httpSettings.method and httpSettings.headers on the h2 transport — Mihomo\'s h2-opts takes only a host and a path (the http masquerade over raw TCP does carry both);
• cipherSuites, curvePreferences, minVersion, disableSystemRoot, masterKeyLog — TLS is not tuned per proxy in Mihomo;
• sockopt tcpNoDelay, tcpUserTimeout, tcpWindowClamp, tcpMaxSeg, V6Only, penetrate, addressPortStrategy, happyEyeballs, customSockopt, keep-alive timers (tcpKeepAliveIdle, tcpKeepAliveInterval) and tcpcongestion; sendThrough, which binds one outbound to a local address;
• pinnedPeerCertificatePublicKeySha256 — it pins the public key while Mihomo\'s fingerprint pins the certificate itself, so one hash cannot stand in for the other;
• wsSettings.useBrowserForwarding, hysteriaSettings.udpIdleTimeout, sockopt.tproxy, a certificate file path in tlsSettings.certificates (inline certificates are carried), tlsSettings.echConfigList given as a URL — Mihomo looks it up in DNS instead — and sockopt.dialerProxy, which only takes effect when a proxy of that exact name is present;
• wsSettings.heartbeatPeriod, grpcSettings.initial_windows_size, realitySettings.spiderX;
• an h3:// resolver is written as https:// — Mihomo takes no HTTP/3 DNS.

When several Xray configs arrive at once, the routing and DNS of the first one are used. A config that states no routing of its own gets the default set instead: a PROXY selector, an AUTO url-test group and rules that send private address ranges direct.

Convert JSON configs received from the VPN provider into formats compatible with other apps. Conversion is configured separately for the "Profiles" and "Subscription" buttons.

Note that not every config can be converted. Read the relevant mode\'s "Conversion limitations" for more detail.

Some Xray features have no equivalents in sing-box, so not every profile can be converted. Unsupported profiles will be skipped.


Transports:
• xhttp, splithttp, mekya, mkcp, meek — no equivalents in sing-box;
• tcp/raw with obfuscation — only none and http are supported;
• quic with obfuscation or headers — sing-box supports raw QUIC only;
• grpc itself converts, but authority and multiMode have no equivalents — the node runs in single mode.

Protocols:
• VLESS with flow xtls-rprx-direct/splice/origin — incompatible with Vision;
• VLESS with encryption ≠ none (e.g. post-quantum);
• VMess with non-standard security (supported: auto/none/zero/aes-128-gcm/chacha20-poly1305/aes-128-ctr);
• security: xtls — deprecated, replaced in modern Xray with tls + flow xtls-rprx-vision;
• Shadowsocks with non-standard method — supported: aes-*-gcm, (x)chacha20-ietf-poly1305, 2022-blake3-aes-128/256-gcm, 2022-blake3-chacha20-poly1305, aes-*-ctr/cfb, chacha20-ietf, xchacha20, rc4-md5, none;
• Shadowsocks with plugins other than obfs-local and v2ray-plugin.

Routing:
• Mux.Cool — incompatible with sing-mux;
• source_geoip — sing-box doesn\'t match geo by source IP;
• balancer.fallbackTag — urltest retries instead of switching;
• balancer.strategy: leastLoad — replaced with urltest (≈ leastPing);
• ext: categories — they name an Xray data file this core cannot read;
• attrs — nothing matches HTTP attributes, so the rule keeps matching without that condition.

Options left out:
• a certificate file path — it names a file on the machine that wrote the config, not on this one; inline certificates are carried;
• a tlsSettings.minVersion or maxVersion outside 1.0–1.3 — the versions themselves are carried;
• sockopt tproxy, tcpNoDelay, tcpUserTimeout, tcpWindowClamp, tcpMaxSeg, tcpcongestion, V6Only, penetrate, addressPortStrategy, happyEyeballs, customSockopt, domainStrategy (the route resolver decides instead);
• pinnedPeerCertSha256 — sing-box pins the public key inside a certificate while Xray pins the certificate itself, so one hash cannot stand in for the other;
• disableSystemRoot, masterKeyLog, wsSettings.heartbeatPeriod, grpcSettings.authority and initial_windows_size, realitySettings.spiderX;
• sockopt keep-alive timers (tcpKeepAliveIdle, tcpKeepAliveInterval) and tlsSettings.curvePreferences — sing-box gained these fields in 1.13, and writing them would stop a 1.12 core loading the configuration;
• wsSettings.useBrowserForwarding, hysteriaSettings.udpIdleTimeout, tlsSettings.echConfigList given as a URL, and sockopt.dialerProxy, which only takes effect when a proxy of that exact name is present;
• verifyPeerCertInNames — sing-box verifies against server_name and has no separate name for the check;
• freedom fragment, redirect and noises; a blackhole HTTP response body — the connection is closed instead.

DNS:
• expectIPs/unexpectedIPs — DNS rules match the request, not the response;
• a per-server queryStrategy — a sing-box server has no field for it, so only the document-level one is carried.

Also carried:
• sendThrough becomes inet4_bind_address or inet6_bind_address, so an outbound pinned to a local address stays pinned.

Routing rules:
The Xray core\'s geosite: and geoip: rules are converted into sing-box rule-sets compatible with the sing-box for Android app and the CLI core. These clients will automatically download the required domain and IP lists from SagerNet repositories.

Note that other sing-box clients (Hiddify, husi, NekoBox, Karing, etc.) usually ignore the routing (rule-set) shipped with imported profiles and use rules configured by the user through the UI.

Below are alternative ways to decrypt links that may help when Happwner can\'t decrypt a link on its own. All of them require extra steps on your part and don\'t guarantee a result.
Link interception, HWID spoofing and profile unlocking
Happ link decryption via its library, intent redirection

Happanion is a companion app for Happwner with functions for rare cases. Features:

• Decrypts happ://crypt5 links using Happ\'s own native library;
• Redirects Happ\'s browser intent links to Happwner instead.

This app installs instead of Happ from Google Play. You\'ll be prompted to remove Happ if it\'s installed.

This decryption method lets you, inside target/patched apps:

• Intercept decrypted links;
• Intercept and substitute the HWID;
• Unlock profile editing in encrypted subscriptions (Happ and v2RayTun);
• Open the Happwner interface with three simultaneous taps.

Allows updating subscriptions in other apps

This feature allows updating subscriptions through any proxy client (Hiddify, husi, v2rayNG and many others). After clicking \"OK\", Happwner will request permission to display notifications, start the service, and copy the link to the clipboard—import it into your app.

Important: enable \"Bypass LAN\" or add a geoip:private rule to direct, otherwise the update will not work when your proxy client\'s connection is active.

This feature allows updating subscriptions through any proxy client (Hiddify, husi, v2rayNG and many others). Tap \"Subscription\" on the main screen, add the copied link to your app, and update the subscription there from now on.

Important: enable \"Bypass LAN\" or add a geoip:private rule to direct, otherwise the update will not work when your proxy client\'s connection is active.
